newsitem.title: UK: NWE high sulphur fuel soft, Russians plentiful.
newsitem.headline: NWE high sulphur fuel soft, Russians plentiful.

text.p: NWE high sulphur fuel oil prices were softer on Monday as crude oil futures weakened and amid continued good supply of Russian cargoes, traders said.
Prompt high sulphur barges were offered at $98 a tonne fob ARA but no business was heard done. Bunker demand was very poor.
High sulphur cargoes weakened in line with barges but no new business was heard done. Utility interest for prompt barrels was heard to be slight.
Russian cargoes remain well supplied, amid signs of flagging refinery interest for straight-run barrels. One regular buyers saw five cargoes available out of Klaipeda in the next week.
One of these, the Moskovskiy Festival, was heard on the water in ARA, carrying an E-4 cargo, after having earlier been offered at a discount to the mean/mean/mean of published quotes.
Another dealer said he thought this had already been sold but had no more details. Buyers felt that published E-4 quotes were currently too high, discouraging refinery buying.
Low sulphur fuel oil was softer in line with futures. Low sulphur barges were offered at $115 fob ARA but no business was heard done.
Low sulphur cargoes were a couple of dollars weaker, and supply was still healthy.
